newsitem.title: GERMANY: Northeast Utilities CEO to retire.
newsitem.headline: Northeast Utilities CEO to retire.

text.p: Northeast Utilities said Thursday Bernard Fox intends to retire as chairman, president and chief executive officer in the second half of this year.
The company, whose nuclear operations have come under sharp criticism by federal regulators and citizens' watchdog groups in the past year, said its board was commencing a search for a successor.

No specific date for Fox's retirement has been set; but it is likely to be sometime between late July, when he turns 55 and becomes eligible to retire, and the end of the year, Northeast Utilities said. Upon his retirement, Fox will continue to assist Northeast Utilities in an advisory capacity for two years.

The utility noted Fox asked the board at its January meeting to accept his request to retire at some point in 1997. The trustees tabled his request at that time but accepted it at a special meeting this week, Northeast Utilities said.
It said Fox has agreed to remain in his position until a successor has been named.
The board is expected to form a search committee at its Feb. 25 meeting but does not expect to complete its search until the second half of this year, the company said.
All three of the company's units at the Millstone nuclear power station in Waterford, Conn., have been closed for safety reasons since March of last year.
Northeast has said it plans to have all three plants ready for restart by early 1998, pending approval by the federal Nuclear Regulatory Commission.
